concepts.def: Quantum tunnelling composite — conducts when squeezed.
Mouldable polymer that softens in hot water.
Wire that glows along its length.
Material that repairs small cracks itself.
Single-layer carbon sheet — strong and conductive.
Ultra-light solid foam with low density.

walkthroughs.body_html: Quantum tunnelling composites contain metal particles in a polymer. When squeezed the particles get close enough for electrons to tunnel, so the material conducts. Used in soft-touch buttons, e-textiles and assistive switches.
Polymorph softens at about 62 °C in hot water and becomes putty-like. It cools to a rigid plastic but can be reheated many times. Designers use it for ergonomic grips and rapid prototypes.
A musician's smart glove uses QTC pads on each fingertip. Pressing a finger sends a signal to a microcontroller that plays a note. Polymorph forms a custom moulded knuckle reinforcement for comfort.
